title: Scheduled atomic cutover drill with rollback safety net and KV-validation harness
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create and validate a repeatable, scheduled failover drill that performs an atomic traffic cutover from primary -> passive region and back, with an emphasis on safe rollback, KV-store validation, SLO observability, circuit breaker calibration, and graduated load-shedding. Goal is a documented, automated harness that can run during a maintenance window with minimal manual intervention and clear success/failure signals.
steps: Stage 0: Pre-drill gating - verify nightly snapshot integrity and backup checksum; confirm control-plane access and target passive region readiness
Stage 1: Canary traffic siphon - route 0.1% traffic to passive region for 15 minutes, check latency p95 and error rate against canary SLOs
Stage 2: KV sync verification - run snapshot-compare job (sha256) and spot-check top-100 hot keys for read-after-write correctness
Stage 3: Incremental ramp - increase siphon to 10% for 30 minutes while validating user-facing SLOs and application-level contracts
Stage 4: Atomic cutover - flip routing layer to passive region (maintenance window) with pre-registered circuit breaker thresholds and a staged load-shedding policy applied to non-critical routes
Stage 5: Post-cutover validation - run end-to-end smoke tests, cross-region consistency checks, and cost/latency telemetry aggregation
Stage 6: Rollback safety net - if any of the defined failure gates are tripped, trigger automated rollback to primary and execute forensic snapshot capture
Stage 7: Restore and restore-validation - after rollback or successful cutover, run a restore-validation harness against the backup snapshot to ensure restorability
Stage 8: Post-mortem instrumentation - collect dashboards, trace samples, and run automated regression detectors against baseline SLOs for SR/DR alerting
acceptance_criteria: Automation: drill can be kicked off from the console or a single CLI script and completes < 2 hours for end-to-end dry run
Safety: rollback must automatically execute if p95 latency increases > 2x baseline or 5xx rate > 0.5% for > 5 minutes
Data integrity: KV snapshot-compare shows zero divergence for the top 1,000 keys and checksum mismatch rate < 0.01%
Observability: a dedicated drill dashboard surfaces SLO deltas, circuit-breaker trips, and load-shedding applied per route
Runbook: a validated step-by-step runbook (Confluence) and GitHub PR with scripts exists and is approved by oncall and platform leads

notes: Decision: We will use the existing Traffic Router's canary weights API (v2) and extend it with a cutover-mode that supports atomic switch + rollback TTL
Trade-off: Full traffic swap provides best fidelity for test but increases blast radius. We mitigate with canary ramp and strict failure gates plus automated rollback
Follow-ups: capture per-tenant shadowing experiments in a separate ticket to evaluate tenant-level failover behavior
PRs: link in 'links' contains current implementation; will split into smaller PRs if rollbacks become hard to reason about
